newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan may make revised offer in WTO telecom talks.
newsitem.headline: Japan may make revised offer in WTO telecom talks.

text.p: Japan may make a revised offer on liberalisation of its telecoms market at a meeting this week of the World Trade Organisation (WTO), but there will be no big change in its stance, a telecoms official said on Monday.

"We will explain in the offer more clearly and explicitly that newcomers to the Japanese market will be ensured interconnections with Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp's local networks," the official at the Posts and Telecommunications Ministry told Reuters.
In December, the ministry's Telecommunications Council came up with new interconnection rules aimed at requiring NTT to give rival phone firms fair access to its networks.
Japan told the WTO in its offer last April that it was ready to lift restrictions on foreign ownership in Japan's telecommunications carriers.
"Japan has made the most advanced offer in this area and we haven't changed this stance," the official said.
The basic telecom talks at the WTO aim to liberalise cross-border investment by telecom companies and end monopolies in the market.
After failing to meet the original deadline of April 1996, talks are continuing at Davos, Switzerland, to meet a new deadline on February 15.
